full_judgment:
3. The properties described in schedule Ka to Uma in the plaint was originally owned and possessed by Jamarat Ali, who by registered deed of heba-bil-ewaz transferred the entire land in favour of his 1st son Rausan Ali in the year 1938, vide, Ext. 1. Jamarat Ali died leaving his son Roushan Ali by his 1st wife and two other sons namely Azibar Ali and Akbar Ali by his second wife. Thereafter Roushan Ali transferred 4.20 acres of land out of the land of the heba-bil-ewaz in favour of his step brothers namely Azibar Ali and Akbar Ali. Thereafter Roushan Ali died leaving widow plaintiff No. 2, a son, plaintiff No. 1 and 2 daughter's plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4. Thereafter Azibar Ali died leaving mother (since dead), full brother defendant No.7 and two sister's defendant Nos. 8 and 9. It is the further case of the plaintiff that the sale deed executed and registered by Roushan Ali in favour of his step-brothers Azibar Ali and Akbar Ali Vide Ext. 'A' is an inactive and inoperative document inasmuch as no consideration money passed and as such the sale deed Ext. 'A' was not acted upon and that Roushan Ali continued to remain in possession of the entire land. It is further stated in the plaint that 1.28 acre of land described in schedule 'Cha' to the plaint out of the entire land of Roushan Ali had wrongly been recorded in the name of the defendants in rent roll khatian and taking advantage of the wrong entry in Rent Roll Khatian defendant threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from said 1.28 acre of land and hence the suit for confirmation of possession on declaration of title thereto. It is further stated that entry in respect of 1.28 acre of land in SA Khatian is without basis and as such it cannot be allowed to stand. Defendant Nos. 1-6 contested the suit by filing written statement. 

 9. In reply to this contention the learned Advocate appearing for the defendants-respondents submits that the 1st appellate Court considered all the aspect of the case and came to correct finding relating to title of suit land. It is further submitted that the 1st appellate Court having scrutinized all the materials on record carefully and rightly, held that the sale deed Ext. 2 is a bonafide document for valuable consideration and on the basis of it defendant Nos. 1-6 have been possessing the suit land. The learned Advocate further submitted that the 1st appellate Court rightly held that no fraud was practiced on Registration Act in as much section 28 (2) of Registration Act empowers the registration authority to register a deed of land lying in different jurisdiction and that the plaintiffs being party to the document cannot raise any objection against the validity of registration. The learned 1st appellate Court having arrived at a finding that Ext. 2 is a bonafide document and that it is acted upon and on this consideration allowed the appeal on setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 11. Admittedly original sale deed Ext. 2 is coming from the custody of plaintiffs. Defendant No. 7 Akbar Ali, one of the vendees of Ext. 2, appeared in the Title Suit and filed separate written statement wherein he admitted that the sale deed Ext. 2 was not acted upon in as much as he failed to pay the consideration money and having failed to pay the consideration money, returned the original sale deed Ext 2 to Roushan Ali who executed and registered Ext. 2. Thus it is evident that defendant No. 7 Akbar Ali who having acquired right, title, interest in the suit land had made a statement in his pleadings which is detrimental to his own interest. Further, it appears that the Ext. 2 was registered in the year 1947. But no dekhalia was produced showing payment of rent from that time onwards. Further it appears that no mutation proceedings were initiated by defendant No. 7 to have the land of Ext. 2 recorded in his name. These are the materials on record which affirmatively prove that the sale deed Ext. 2 which is coming from the custody of the plaintiff appellant was not in fact active document and did not operate to pass right, title, interest in favour of the transferee Akbar Ali. In this connection the observation made by the 1st appellate: 

 Court relating to possession of the land in suit needs to be referred. The learned 1st appellate Court stated in his judgment that PW 4 Akbar Ali admitted possession of defendant Nos. 1-6 in the suit land. But this PW 4 Akbar Ali does not own any land in the vicinity of the suit land. So he is not supposed to know the possession of the suit land and competent to speak about possession. Further it appears that no evidence has been led to prove that payment of consideration money was made to the executants Roushan Ali. Defendants side wants to take advantage of the sale deed Ext. 2 so the onus lies on them to prove that consideration money of Ext 2 was duly paid and that sale deed Ext. 2 was followed by delivery of possession. The plea was that sale deed Ext. 2 is an active and bonafide document and that consideration was duly passed but no evidence in this regard was adduced by the defence side. Production of the original sale deed Ext 2 from the custody of the plaintiffs appellant lends support to this contention that when Roushan Ali's step-brothers Ajibar and Akbar failed to pay the consideration returned the original deed to Roushan Ali who having received back the original deed from his step-brothers Ajibur and Akbar retained possession of the land covered by Ext. 2 and on the death of Roushan Ali the custody of the original deed Ext. 2 passed to plaintiffs as the heirs of Roushan Ali. It has already been pointed out that no dakhilas showing payment of rent for 4.28 acres of land was produced by the defence side. Nor any mutation proceeding was initiated.
